note: Submodule of tmgmt_deepl. Manages DeepL glossaries in Drupal via content entities deepl_glossary (classic single-pair; base table tmgmt_deepl_glossary; fields label, source_lang, target_lang, tmgmt_translator, glossary_id, ready, entry_count, entries [field type deepl_glossary_item with subject/definition]), deepl_ml_glossary and deepl_ml_glossary_dictionary (multilingual). Configure route is the overview View view.tmgmt_deepl_glossary.page_1; fetch form at /admin/tmgmt/deepl_glossaries/fetch; dedicated permissions (administer/add/edit/delete deepl_glossary entities, edit deepl_glossary glossary entries, access deepl_glossary overview); API service classes DeeplGlossaryApi/DeeplMultilingualGlossaryApi. Syncing/creating glossaries ON DeepL needs the parent module's auth key, so ALL medium/hard cases are grounded in the local deepl_glossary content entity (create/read/add entries does NOT call DeepL). Scripts key on the entity label (ids autoincrement) and delete their own Eval/Legal/Product glossaries.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal tmgmt_deepl_glossary submodule let me do, and how does it help DeepL translations?
evals.expected_output: It lets you create and manage DeepL glossaries (lists of source->target term pairs) in Drupal so DeepL translates those terms consistently, supporting classic single-language-pair glossaries and DeepL multilingual glossaries.

evals.prompt: Which entities and field type does tmgmt_deepl_glossary add for storing glossary data?
evals.expected_output: It adds content entities deepl_glossary (classic single-pair), deepl_ml_glossary and deepl_ml_glossary_dictionary (multilingual), plus a field type deepl_glossary_item whose items store a subject (source term) and definition (target term).

evals.prompt: What permission controls full administration of DeepL glossaries in tmgmt_deepl_glossary, and how can a non-admin translator be allowed just to edit glossary term entries?
evals.expected_output: 'administer deepl_glossary entities' grants full glossary administration (it is the entity admin_permission). Give a translator 'edit deepl_glossary glossary entries' (and 'access deepl_glossary overview') to let them edit term entries without full admin rights.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a DeepL glossary labelled 'Eval Brand Glossary'. Inspect the live glossary entity and tell me which source and target languages it translates between.
evals.expected_output: It translates English (en) to German (de): the deepl_glossary 'Eval Brand Glossary' has source_lang=en, target_lang=de.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a DeepL glossary labelled 'Eval Terms Glossary'. Inspect its entries and tell me the target-language translation it stores for the source term 'invoice'.
evals.expected_output: It stores 'Rechnung' for 'invoice': the deepl_glossary 'Eval Terms Glossary' has an entries item with subject=invoice, definition=Rechnung.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the tmgmt_deepl_glossary module to create a DeepL glossary entity labelled 'Legal Terms FR' that translates from English (en) to French (fr). Apply the change to the live site. (You do not need to sync it to DeepL.)
evals.expected_output: Create and save a deepl_glossary content entity with label 'Legal Terms FR', source_lang en, target_lang fr. Verify checks such an entity exists with source_lang=en and target_lang=fr.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a DeepL glossary labelled 'Product Glossary' (English to German) that currently has no term entries. Add a glossary term entry mapping the source term 'product' to the German translation 'Produkt'. Apply the change to the live glossary.
evals.expected_output: Append a deepl_glossary_item to the 'Product Glossary' entity's entries field with subject 'product' and definition 'Produkt', and save. Verify checks an entry product -> Produkt exists.
